rationale: Record a browser-process lifecycle timing fix and test-only deadline changes for Pulp's real-browser capture. browser_process.mjs bounds its teardown waits with a helper that clears its timer, so a capture process exits when cleanup finishes instead of holding a spent six-second bound (a trivial capture drops from about 12.3 s to 7.7 s wall), and a launch now waits up to 5 s rather than 1.5 s on POSIX for its lifecycle guardian to publish custody, matching Windows. The *.integration.test.mjs cases take one 30 s capture deadline and a derived case timeout from capture_integration_support.mjs instead of per-case 15-20 s literals. Captured pages, DOM snapshots, pixels, sidecars, design ingest, rendering, packaging, browser selection and pinning, custody verification and signalling, the accepted expansion boundary, and Vellum source authority are unchanged.
tests: tools/scripts/confirm_failure.sh on waitAtMost clearTimeout and on the guardian-stop call site (CONFIRMED both)
